title: World roundup: Drone attack in Kuwait kills 2 Italians, Guinea-Bissau delays vote to 2028, Trump says he pressed Putin
key_points: Kuwait and Italy say an Iranian drone attack killed two Italian technicians in Kuwait; Iran denies any role.
Guinea-Bissau's military rulers moved elections from December 6 to November 2028.
Trump says he asked Putin to pull back military aggression across Europe and hopes for a quick Ukraine deal.
The Iran-related crisis keeps shipping in the Strait of Hormuz under threat, which affects fuel prices worldwide.
content:
Here are the biggest world stories from the last 24 hours, in simple words.

1. Kuwait: drone attack kills two Italian workers

Two Italian technicians were killed on Thursday when drones hit a military air-defence station in Kuwait, according to Kuwait's defence ministry and Italy's foreign minister, Antonio Tajani. The two men worked for Rheinmetall Italia, a defence company. Tajani said two other people were injured: a Pakistani national and a Kuwaiti army captain.

Kuwait and Italy blamed Iran. Iran denied it. Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi told his Kuwaiti and Italian counterparts that Iran had "no role or involvement whatsoever", The New Arab reported. Iran offered a joint investigation. The claims could not be independently confirmed.

The attack came as the war that began in February between Iran and the US and Israel continues to disrupt the Gulf. ABC News (Australia) reported that two more ships were hit in the Strait of Hormuz on the same day; the UK maritime agency UKMTO said both crews were safe.

Why it matters: many Kenyans work in Gulf countries such as Kuwait, Saudi Arabia and the UAE. Trouble around Hormuz also pushes up the cost of fuel and transport, including in Kenya.

2. Guinea-Bissau: military rulers delay elections by two years

Guinea-Bissau's military government has postponed presidential and parliamentary elections that were due on December 6. The new date is November 26, 2028, according to AP and RTÉ. Al Jazeera also reported the delay.

The decree was signed by transitional President General Horta Inta-a on Thursday, exactly one year after the army took power. It said the "technical, material and financial conditions" for a vote were not in place. The military seized power in November 2025, three days after an election, removing President Umaro Sissoco Embaló before results were announced. The West African bloc ECOWAS had asked for a short transition, Al Jazeera said.

Why it matters: it is one more West African country where soldiers are staying in power longer than promised.

3. Trump says he asked Putin to "pull back" in Europe

US President Donald Trump said on Thursday that he asked Russian President Vladimir Putin to pull back military aggression against territories across Europe. They met last week in Shenzhen, China, at the APEC leaders' meeting, Reuters reported.

Writing on Truth Social, Trump said he hopes Russia and Ukraine can make a deal soon. "I really believe this is a strong possibility," he wrote. He also said the biggest obstacle is the deep dislike between Putin and Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky. There are no formal peace talks at the moment, according to the Reuters report.

The Kremlin said no decision has been made on whether Putin will attend the G20 summit in Florida on December 14–15.

4. EU leaders argue over the next long-term budget

European Union leaders met on Thursday to discuss the bloc's budget for 2028 to 2034, worth nearly €1.6 trillion, and money for Ukraine, The Standard (Hong Kong) reported. No final deal was reported.

Why it matters: the EU is one of Kenya's biggest trade and aid partners, so its budget choices affect support for Africa.

5. US: Thanksgiving storm cuts power on the East Coast

A strong storm hit the US East Coast on Thanksgiving Day, with wind gusts of up to 70 mph (112 km/h), The Standard (Hong Kong) reported. Falling trees and power lines left hundreds of thousands of customers without electricity, and flights were disrupted.

Why it matters: Kenyans in the US travelling this holiday weekend should check their flight status and local power updates before leaving home.
